hook.text: The Netherlands moves 27% of all trips by bicycle. The secret is infrastructure.

buildup.text: Separated cycle tracks keep bikes away from cars — physical barriers, not just paint.

discovery.text: Protected intersections give cyclists their own signal phase and turning lanes.

twist.text: Paint-only bike lanes have crash rates five times higher than separated facilities.

climax.text: Copenhagen's Cykelslangen is a cycling bridge — elevated, heated, and snowplowed.

punchline.text: Build it safe and people will ride. Paint alone isn't enough.

quiz.question: Why are separated cycle tracks safer than painted bike lanes?
options: Cyclists travel faster on separated tracks due to better pavement
Physical barriers prevent vehicle intrusion, reducing crash rates significantly
Separated tracks are only used in areas with no car traffic

details.summary: Bicycle infrastructure includes protected bike lanes, cycle tracks, shared-use paths, bike parking, and intersection treatments designed to provide safe, convenient cycling separate from motor vehicle traffic.
details.whyItMatters: Cycling provides zero-emission transportation that improves public health and reduces congestion. Protected infrastructure is the primary factor determining whether people choose to cycle for daily transportation.
takeaways: Protected bike lanes increase cycling rates by 75-200% on corridors where built
Intersection design is the most critical safety element for bicycle infrastructure
Dutch junction design separates turning conflicts between bikes and motor vehicles

faq.question: Why is physical separation from traffic so important for cycling?
faq.answer: Studies consistently show that fear of traffic is the primary barrier preventing people from cycling. Painted bike lanes provide minimal safety improvement.

faq.question: How do protected intersections work for bicycle safety?
faq.answer: Protected intersections use corner refuge islands that set cyclists back from the intersection, making them visible to turning drivers. Separate signal phases give cyclists dedicated crossing time without motor vehicle conflicts. This Dutch-inspired design reduces intersection crashes dramatically.
